arabic_alphabet.title: Alif (ا)
arabic_alphabet.description: The first letter of the Arabic alphabet

content.title: Introduction to Alif
content.body: Alif (ا) is the first letter of the Arabic alphabet. It is a long vowel that makes an 'aa' sound. Unlike English vowels, Alif is always written and never silent.

content.title: Listen to Alif
content.body: Listen carefully to how Alif is pronounced. It should come from deep in your throat with an open mouth.

content.title: Practice Saying Alif
content.body: Now it's your turn. Record yourself saying Alif and compare it to the correct pronunciation.

content.title: Identify Alif
content.body: Which of these is the letter Alif?
content.explanation: Alif (ا) is a tall vertical line, the simplest letter in the Arabic alphabet.

content.title: Introduction to Ba
content.body: Ba (ب) makes a 'b' sound like in 'book'. It has a rounded bottom shape with a single dot underneath.

content.title: Listen to Ba
content.body: Listen to the Ba sound. Notice how it sounds exactly like the English 'b' sound.

content.title: Ba in Words
content.body: Try to identify Ba in these common words.

content.title: Test Your Knowledge
content.body: How many dots does Ba have?
content.explanation: Ba (ب) has exactly one dot below the letter.

content.title: Introduction to Ta
content.body: Ta (ت) makes a 't' sound. It has the same base shape as Ba but with two dots above instead of one below.

content.title: Listen to Ta
content.body: The Ta sound is similar to English 't' but pronounced with the tongue touching the back of the upper teeth.

content.title: Ba vs Ta
content.body: What is the difference between Ba (ب) and Ta (ت)?
options: The number and position of dots
content.correctAnswer: The number and position of dots
content.explanation: Ba has one dot below, while Ta has two dots above. The base shape is the same.

tajweed_basics.title: What is Tajweed?
tajweed_basics.description: Understanding the importance of proper Quran recitation

content.title: Introduction
content.body: Tajweed (تجويد) comes from the Arabic root meaning 'to make better' or 'to improve'. It refers to the rules that govern the proper pronunciation of the Quran. Learning Tajweed helps us recite the Quran as it was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

content.title: Why Learn Tajweed?
content.body: Allah says in the Quran: 'And recite the Quran with measured recitation' (73:4). Proper recitation preserves the meaning and beauty of Allah's words. Mistakes in pronunciation can sometimes change the meaning entirely.

content.title: Check Understanding
content.body: What does 'Tajweed' mean?
content.explanation: Tajweed means to improve or perfect, referring to perfecting the recitation of the Quran.

tajweed_basics.title: Makharij (Articulation Points)
tajweed_basics.description: Learn where sounds originate in the mouth and throat

content.title: What are Makharij?
content.body: Makharij (مخارج) are the points of articulation - the specific places in your mouth, throat, and nasal passages where each Arabic letter's sound originates. There are 17 main articulation points.

content.title: The Five Main Areas
content.body:
1. Al-Jawf (الجوف) - The empty space in mouth/throat
2. Al-Halq (الحلق) - The throat
3. Al-Lisan (اللسان) - The tongue
4. Ash-Shafatan (الشفتان) - The lips
5. Al-Khayshum (الخيشوم) - The nasal passage

content.title: Throat Letters
content.body: Listen to the letters that come from the throat: ء ه ع ح غ خ
content.arabicText: ء ه ع ح غ خ

content.title: What is Noon Sakinah?
content.body: Noon Sakinah (نْ) is a Noon with sukoon (no vowel). The Tanween (ً ٍ ٌ) also follows these rules because it sounds like Noon at the end. There are four rules that apply depending on the letter that follows.

content.title: The Four Rules
content.body:
1. Idhgham (إدغام) - Merging
2. Iqlab (إقلاب) - Changing
3. Ikhfa (إخفاء) - Hiding
4. Izhar (إظهار) - Clear pronunciation

content.title: Test Yourself
content.body: How many rules apply to Noon Sakinah?
content.explanation: There are four rules: Idhgham, Iqlab, Ikhfa, and Izhar.

content.title: Introduction
content.body: The Five Pillars of Islam are the foundation of Muslim life. They are the testimony of faith, prayer, giving zakat, fasting during Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to Makkah.

content.title: 1. Shahada - Declaration of Faith
content.body: The Shahada is the Muslim declaration of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.' This is the most fundamental expression of Islamic beliefs.
content.arabicText: لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله
content.transliteration: La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad rasul Allah

content.title: 2. Salah - Prayer
content.body: Muslims pray five times a day: Fajr (dawn), Dhuhr (noon), Asr (afternoon), Maghrib (sunset), and Isha (night). Prayer provides a direct link between the worshipper and Allah.

content.title: 3. Zakat - Charity
content.body: Zakat is giving 2.5% of one's savings to those in need. It purifies wealth and helps build a just society.

content.title: 4. Sawm - Fasting
content.body: During Ramadan, Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. Fasting teaches self-discipline, sacrifice, and empathy for those less fortunate.

content.title: 5. Hajj - Pilgrimage
content.body: Every Muslim who is physically and financially able must make the pilgrimage to Makkah at least once in their lifetime. It takes place in the 12th month of the Islamic calendar.

content.title: Test Your Knowledge
content.body: Which pillar involves giving 2.5% of savings?
content.explanation: Zakat is the pillar of giving 2.5% of one's savings to those in need.
